# Poodle Circle

> Poodle Circle is a practical, friendly guide for people living with toy poodles, especially during the first 30 days after bringing a puppy home.

Poodle Circle (https://poodlecircle.com/) is a toy poodle owner guide and community site. A new owner starts the first 30 days, then opens the one problem in front of them. Instagram (https://www.instagram.com/poodle.circle/) carries a question or a short clip outward. The answers stay on this site.

Written for everyday owners. These are owner routines, not veterinary care, and not a place to sell puppies or promote breeding. A puppy who is weak, collapsing, or refusing food should see a veterinarian. Principles: https://poodlecircle.com/#principles

There is no named author. The guides have not been reviewed by a veterinarian. Updated dates on each guide are the editorial dates. Poodle Circle is not a clinic.

Every care guide ends with: Start your First 30 Days → https://poodlecircle.com/first-30-days/

## Start here

- Homepage: https://poodlecircle.com/
- First week and first month, week by week: https://poodlecircle.com/first-30-days/
- Free First 30 Days guide PDF, a simple day-by-day checklist, no email: https://poodlecircle.com/assets/first-30-days-kit.pdf
- The long guide, for the night you are in: https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/

## New puppy

- New toy poodle, first month: https://poodlecircle.com/first-30-days/
- Toy poodle first night: one quiet room, a toilet trip, then sleep. Skip visitors and a house tour. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#day-1
- Toy poodle first week: https://poodlecircle.com/first-30-days/#week-1
- Toy poodle first month, week by week: https://poodlecircle.com/first-30-days/
- What to buy before bringing home a toy poodle: food, bowls, a bed, a crate or pen, a harness, an ID tag, and an enzyme cleaner. Shampoo and extra toys can wait. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#before
- Toy poodle puppy schedule: toilet, a meal or a short play, then a nap, in the same order. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#routine
- Toy poodle puppy sleeping in the first month: they sleep a lot. If they go wild, try a rest, not another game. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#sleep
- Toy poodle puppy outside: day 1 is one toilet trip, then back inside. Longer walks wait until a harness stays on. Once you are out, carry steep stairs, coat them early, and keep them close in open country. https://poodlecircle.com/stairs/
- Toy poodle puppy questions: the long guide answers the first-month questions, then each problem has its own page. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#faq
- Toy poodle socialisation (also searched as socialization): calm exposure, not a parade of strangers. Vaccination timing belongs with a veterinarian. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#social
- First night checklist: toilet trip, one quiet room, sleep, no visitors. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#first-night
- I just brought home a toy poodle. What should I do today? One quiet room, a toilet trip, and sleep. https://poodlecircle.com/first-30-days/#week-1
- I've had my toy poodle for one week. What should we work on now? A minute of alone time, then brushing, then the harness indoors. https://poodlecircle.com/first-30-days/#week-2
- Toy poodle puppy crying at night after they had settled: a last toilet, one calm check, then stop answering. https://poodlecircle.com/night-waking/

## Behaviour

- Toy poodle barking: reward one quiet second away from the door. Shouting adds noise. https://poodlecircle.com/apartment-barking/
- Toy poodle separation anxiety: crying at the start of practice can be a habit. Distress that grows needs a shorter practice and help, not two hours. https://poodlecircle.com/alone-time/#faq
- Toy poodle biting: stop moving your hands, redirect to a toy, praise the toy. Wildness may be overtired. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#biting
- Toy poodle zoomies: another hallway lap often winds them up. A short sniff and a puzzle, then stop while they can settle. https://poodlecircle.com/apartment-barking/#faq
- Toy poodle alone time: start in seconds. Two hours is a later step. https://poodlecircle.com/alone-time/
- Toy poodle crate training: the crate is a bed, not a penalty. Door open first. Never a punishment. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#crate

## Grooming

- How often to brush a toy poodle, and how to line brush: ears, armpits, and behind the legs every day. A full line brush several times a week. If the comb stops, you stop. https://poodlecircle.com/line-brushing/
- Toy poodle tear stains: wipe with water, dry the fur, keep hair under the eyes short. No whitening drops. https://poodlecircle.com/tear-stains/
- Toy poodle grooming schedule: comb to the skin at home, salon on a calendar. https://poodlecircle.com/home-brushing/
- Toy poodle mats: if the comb will not pass, book a groomer. Do not cut a mat out with scissors. https://poodlecircle.com/line-brushing/
- Best brush for toy poodles: a metal comb with wide teeth and narrow teeth. A slicker is not a substitute. This site does not rank products. https://poodlecircle.com/line-brushing/#faq

## Everyday life

- Toy poodle harness: two fingers, a lift test, not a collar. https://poodlecircle.com/harness/
- Toy poodle stairs, cold, and hawks: carry steep flights, coat them early, keep them close in open country. https://poodlecircle.com/stairs/
- Toy poodle travelling: short trips, a carrier or a secure restraint, never loose in the car. https://poodlecircle.com/30daysguide/#car
- Toy poodle apartment and exercise: a 10 to 20 minute sniff walk and a puzzle, not another hallway lap. https://poodlecircle.com/apartment-barking/
- Toy poodle teeth: toothpaste made for dogs, a few teeth, stop while they are calm. Not human toothpaste. https://poodlecircle.com/teeth/

## This week's question

My toy poodle cries every time I leave the room. What worked for you?

Leave for less time than they can already manage. Toilet first, a safe chew, a calm goodbye, and come back before the noise turns into panic. If the crying gets worse as you stay away longer, shorten the practice and ask a vet or a qualified trainer.

Full answer: https://poodlecircle.com/alone-time/#cries

## Not care guides

- The spoiled quiz is a named break from puppy homework. The result is a nickname, a spoilage score, and something to share. It is not a diagnosis. https://poodlecircle.com/quiz/
- Poodle Parkour is a tiny jump game, not a care guide. https://poodlecircle.com/games/poodle-parkour/
